S(n)=\sum_{i=1}^{n} \big((i \bmod 1\,000\,000)+1\big)^2 \pmod{10^9+7}

## What the code does

- `M = 1'000'000` (hardcoded as the array size).

The loop runs `n` times, so the time complexity is \(O(n)\). If `n` is large (e.g., \(10^9\) or \(10^{18}\)), this will be far too slow.

The sequence  
\[
a_i = ((i \bmod M)+1)^2

- `sumPeriod` = sum of \(k^2\) for \(k=1\) to \(M\) (since the values in one period are a permutation of \(1^2, 2^2, \dots, M^2\)).
- The total sum is then  
  \[
  S(n) = \left\lfloor \frac{n}{M} \right\rfloor \cdot \text{sumPeriod} + \text{sum of the first } (n \bmod M) \text{ terms of the period}.
  \]

This reduces the time complexity from \(O(n)\) to \(O(M)\) for precomputation (or even \(O(1)\) with the sum-of-squares formula) and \(O(1)\) per query.
